title: Chapter 2: At This Rate, You'll Never Be Able To Become The Kind Of Person Who Gets Taken Care Of, You Know? 1
content: “――――So that’s what happened.” After coming home from school, I changed into my room clothes and was alone in my room. I had casually eaten dinner and taken a bath, and now I was sitting in my chair wearing headphones, facing the computer on my desk, engaged in a voice chat conversation.

By the way, the person on the other end wasn’t one of my childhood friends or school friends. Well, I guess you could call them a friend, but it’s more accurate to say they’re not someone I meet in real life at school. As promised before, I was about to start a game with someone over the internet.
“My classmates are all ganging up on me, tearing me apart. I haven’t done anything wrong, but they’re calling me a fiend and a heartless bastard…” I said.

“That’s just awful…” The voice agreeing with me was female. Thanks to the headphones costing over a hundred thousand yen, her voice was crystal clear and beautiful, carrying emotion as well. I could definitely hear sympathy for me in her tone.
We had already launched the game, but during the brief preparation time, I was telling her about the events of the past few days.
“Or maybe I did something wrong too?”
“No, I don’t think so. Trying to corner one person with a whole group—that’s obviously the wrong side. I think you haven’t done anything bad, Kuzuma-kun.”
By the way, Kuzuma is my handle name. It’s just a simple combination of my family name Kuzuhara and my given name Kazuma, but I kind of like it. Simple is best. I prefer things straightforward.
“Thank you, Harukaze-san. Just hearing that saves me.”
“I’m always on your side, Kuzuma-kun. If you ever have trouble, feel free to talk to me, okay? I’ll do my best for you.”

Harukaze-san and I met through the game, but her voice was very pleasant to listen to, transparent and comforting, and just talking to her healed my heart. You could call it pure and genuine. Even though our connection was only through the game, she listened seriously to my story. I can say with certainty that there aren’t many people like her.
I liked her enough to think it would be amazing to parasitize her and be supported by her.
“Harukaze-san…”
“Hehe. Was that a little cheesy? But don’t forget, it’s the truth. After all, I’m older than you, Kazuma-kun.”

She laughed, but I thought the last words were serious. I’d heard before that Harukaze-san is one year older than me, a third-year high school student. So calling herself my ‘older sister’ is correct, but it’s a shame she’s too close in age to actually support me financially.

Well, I’m being supported by Setsuna and Arisa, who are the exception. Unless you’re in a special position like an idol, very few high school students can make a lot of money. Harukaze-san is a good person, but I’m not rotten enough to try to parasitize someone living an ordinary life. I still have at least a minimum sense of decency.
“Thanks. I’ll remember that.”
“Yeah! …Ah, it’s about to start. Ready?”
“Ah, wait a moment… here, here.”
When the conversation paused and the game was about to start, I hurriedly opened my item inventory.
“All right… Harukaze-san, I want to send you something, so could you open the channel?”
“Huh? A gift?”
“Yes… okay, I just sent it. Could you check if it arrived?”
“Ah, it just came… huh, this is…”
I heard her gasp on the other end. It seemed to have arrived safely.
“Please use this for the quest. With this, it should be a lot easier.”
“But this is a paid item, right? And a gacha-limited one at that? You’re a high schooler too, Kazuma-kun. It’s bad to receive something like this.”
“Don’t worry about it. You listened to my complaints and always help me out, so this is like a thank-you.”
She’s helped me a lot. This is a pure gift filled with gratitude. No ulterior motives or hidden intentions.
“But…”
“It’s really okay. Actually, I got it by randomly pulling with tickets, so it’s basically free. I won’t use it, so it’s more efficient if you use it.”
Well, in reality, I spent quite a bit on gacha and ended up broke. But now I’m fine thanks to the money Arisa gave me, so I truly don’t want her to worry.
“...If that’s the case, I’ll accept it. Thanks.”
“You’re welcome.”
“Ah, I was going to help you, but it turned out the other way around. I’ll repay you properly someday.”
“Don’t worry about it.”
“Nope. I’m your older sister, after all. Besides, I’m actually a bit amazing, you know? I’ll make sure you realize that someday.”
“Haha, what’s that supposed to mean? Well, I won’t get my hopes up.”
“Ah, that’s mean!”
Teasing an older sister is surprisingly fun. After that, while soothing and comforting Harukaze-san who was sulking and acting like an older sister, I forgot reality and just enjoyed the game.
A few days passed since that chaotic encounter.
Maybe consulting with Harukaze-san paid off. Despite everything, I had completely regained my momentum and was heading to school with a clear heart.
The sky, approaching May, was still holding onto winter’s chill but was clear and blue. Just walking felt good. On days like this, I couldn’t help but hum a tune. Actually, I sang.
“Hum hum hum~♪ I don’t wanna work~♪ Living off playing is the best~♪”
Ah, life is wonderful! I once read in a book that when people are affirmed that they’re not wrong, they gain confidence—and that’s exactly it.
The kanji for ‘person’ () is made by supporting each other, but if possible, I’d like to be supported all the time and live as I please. Of course, I have zero intention of supporting anyone else.
With that lighthearted mood, I approached school. Students wearing the same uniform began appearing here and there on the way, some forming groups with friends.
Ah, how beautiful friendship is. Friendship is wonderful!
“Isn’t that the infamous Kuz—?”
“Yeah, the one who’s feeding money to those idols…”
“Ugh, what kind of mentality is that? Normal people can’t do that.”
“Well, if you had a normal mentality, you wouldn’t be taking money from childhood friends in the first place…”
“True.”
“Man, Kuz is amazing.”
Correction. When people gather, they talk about nothing decent.
Friendships built on gossiping about others’ faults should just crack and shatter quickly.
“Damn it, everyone’s ganging up on me and calling me scum. What did I even do…”
I couldn’t help but curse, but I think it’s understandable.
For some reason, my notoriety at school had skyrocketed in the past few days.
If it were a good rumor about girls wanting to support me financially, that’d be great, but for some reason, I was being treated like scum.
“I’m just receiving the rightful rewards from Setsuna and the others as a childhood friend…”
This world is always full of unfairness.
As I was lamenting the world, a figure approached me.
“Yo, you must be the infamous Kuzuhara, huh?”
He suddenly threw his arm around my shoulder and got close, calling my name.
He was quite handsome, but his skin was tanned, hair dyed brown, and he had multiple piercings in his ears.
Our school allows uniform customization and has lax rules, but it’s still a prestigious school.
A flashy guy like him is rare. And he’s the playboy type.
His uniform was worn sloppily, and I could faintly smell perfume, which I really disliked.
Putting that aside, I was instantly annoyed by his overly familiar attitude and replied curtly.
“What the hell? Who are you?”
“Hey, Kuzuhara, you’re a second-year, right? I’m a third-year, so use honorifics. It’s common sense.”
If you’re going to talk about common sense, first consider the person you’re bothering unilaterally.
Looks like he’s no good.
“Sorry about that. Is this better?”
“Yeah. I’m kind, so I’ll forgive you this time, but next time won’t be so easy. I’ll introduce myself: I’m Hijiri Renji. Ever heard of me?”
“Nope. Not interested.”
I answered immediately. He won’t support me financially, so I have no reason to look him up.
But Renji, smiling strangely at my reply, said,
“Heh, right. I agree. I’m not interested in guys either. Maybe we get along better than I thought.”
“What do you want to say? I’m worried about people watching, so please back off quickly.”
His smirk wasn’t exactly charming, but since he was handsome, it still looked decent, which made me feel weird.
If a plain-looking guy did this, it wouldn’t look good, proving that equality doesn’t exist in this world.
Putting aside that pointless reality escape, I wanted to quickly end this clearly troublesome situation of being bothered by a flashy upperclassman, but it seemed that wouldn’t happen.
“You’re impatient. Think about why I’m interested in you. I obviously want to talk. Just stick around a bit more.”
His grip tightened. Despite his light tone, he had no intention of letting me go.
It was hard to tell under his blazer, but he seemed fairly well-built.
Struggling would only make things worse, so I reluctantly decided to listen.
“Fine. So, what do you want from me, senpai?”
“Just curious. About how you’re ‘winning over’ those idols.”
He twisted his mouth lecherously and continued.

“You know our school has all the members of ‘Damenzu,’ right? They’re famous active idols. I want to be with those girls. I was getting tired of ordinary women. The higher the hurdle, the more it fires me up. My goal is to take down the members of ‘Damenzu’ one by one. It’s like a little game.”
“Is that so.”

“Just as I was deciding who to go for first, I heard rumors about you. Of course, you beat me to it, but I was honestly pissed that you got both Takanashi and Tsukishiro. I didn’t think anyone else could win them over.”
“Sounds like tough luck.”
“Yeah, I was totally outplayed. So today, I’m seeing you as a rival and came to pay my respects. Remember me, Kuzuhara.”
What a nuisance. I’m just being bothered unilaterally.
It’s not profitable and I’ve caught the attention of a troublesome guy.
“Yeah, whatever.”

“You’ve been pretty indifferent. Well, I like you since you’re not scared of me. I’ll let you have those two. In exchange, I get third-year Harukaze Mai and first-year Tachibana Ruri. That’s fair, right?”
Hey, don’t tell me that. I can’t really respond to that.
I can’t say it’s unrelated, but I’m at a loss for how to react.
I nodded casually. The less I get involved, the better. Better to end this nuisance quickly.
“Sure, if you’re that confident, good luck.”
“Yeah. But I still have something to ask you.”
I thought I was free, but apparently not.
Still grinning, Renji leaned in closer.
“Hey, that’s too close. Back off.”
“How did you win over those two? I want you to teach me.”
This senpai clearly doesn’t listen.
I wonder how he’s popular. Probably because he’s good-looking.
He’s way too close and annoying, but the girls around him are blushing and squealing, making me feel even more uncomfortable.
I wanted to end this quickly, but it seemed impossible.

“You’re impatient. Tell me already. How was it? Holding those idols must’ve been amazing, right? Mashiro’s big boobs are tempting, but those two have great figures and must feel nice to hold. Above all, the sense of conquest and superiority from hugging idols must be incredible. Just imagining it drives me crazy.”
Renji licked his lips with a lewd smile. Like a carnivore eyeing prey, I sighed.
“I didn’t hold them. They’re just childhood friends.”
“Don’t lie. It’s already a rumor in our grade. The real scumbag who touched two idols, Kuzuhara Kazuma. I’m not well-regarded either, but you beat me.”
What kind of nickname is that? That’s too harsh.
I could sue for defamation. I’m already tired this morning.
“I told you, it’s not true. I haven’t touched them.”
“That can’t be. Any guy would want those beautiful girls—”
Before Renji finished, I interrupted.
“They’re certainly cute idols, but I’m not close to them for their looks or bodies.”
“Huh? Don’t tell me you’re going to talk about personality or inner qualities.”
Renji frowned, clearly disgusted. I knew what he wanted to say, but he was completely off base.
“If that’s the case, I’m disappointed. I don’t want to hear such virgin nonsense. Stop being so stubborn.”
“No, I’m not stubborn, and I’m not trying to say that.”
“Huh? Then what is it? You just keep denying everything. I’m serious here. Kuzuhara, be honest.”
Renji seemed irritated, and I was getting fed up too.
“Fine. I’ll tell you.”
I didn’t want to deal with him anymore, so I decided to be honest.
“That’s more like it. That’s what a man should do. So, what exactly did you teach those two—”
“Money.”
I said it bluntly. Renji looked at me dumbfounded.
“Don’t you get it? I’ll say it again.”
Since he seemed clueless, I declared clearly.
“My goal is the money they earn as idols.”
“I don’t care about looks or bodies. I just want the money they make as idols.”
“Huh? W-why money?”
“Let me ask you instead. What are your plans for the future? Will you go to college and then work?”
“Uh? Yeah, that’s right? Uh? Uh?”
Hearing that, I sighed deeply. I might as well say I was disappointed.
“Ha… I thought so. Despite your flashy looks, you’re just like everyone else—a pitiful corporate slave. I’m the one who’s disappointed.”
“W-what are you saying? Seriously, what are you saying!?”
Renji still didn’t get it.
I didn’t have to explain, but since I probably won’t see him again, I figured it wouldn’t hurt.
“No matter how much you sleep around, satisfying your lust doesn’t make money. Not realizing that is pathetic.”
“Instead of satisfying desires that way, it’s better to have girls work for the free time you get. That way, you’re supported and can live playing without working.”
Renji’s eyes widened in shock. His grip loosened, so I took the chance to shake off his hand.
“Ah!”
“Well, excuse me. I’ve realized there’s no benefit talking to you.”
“W-wait!”
No one stops when told that.
“Senpai, it’s fine to enjoy girls’ bodies, but you can’t become a true winner or someone who’s taken care of like that, you know?”
Leaving the confused flashy senpai behind, I walked away.
“Hmph, nailed it…”
Despite the annoyance, I reached the classroom door without incident.
I was annoyed by the morning hassle, but I felt great having delivered my final line.
I’m a super handsome guy, so I usually look good no matter what I do, but chances to act cool like that don’t come often.
In that sense, I might even thank that flashy senpai a bit.
Still feeling refreshed, I opened the door, but my mood immediately plummeted.
“Morning, everyone…”
“Look who’s here, Kuzuhara Kazuma!”
“Ugh, again?”
I’ve heard that line so many times this week.
Waiting for me was Ijuuin, standing with arms crossed and a smug look.
I don’t mind her acting high and mighty, but her wavy blonde hair reflected the sunlight glaringly, hurting my eyes. I felt like I was being burned in more ways than one.
“Ugh, not ‘ugh’! Today I’ll settle this! No matter if heaven forgives your misdeeds, I won’t!”
“Yeah, yeah, good morning, good morning. The blonde princess is lively as always. I envy your energy.”
“Hey, why are you trying to just walk past me!?”
I thought seeing something so flashy first thing in the morning was unpleasant and tried to ignore her and head to my seat, but that was a mistake.
“Well, I just got here and want to put my stuff on my desk…”
“You’re trying to run away, aren’t you? No way!”
Ijuuin blocked my way like she wouldn’t let me escape.
Not even letting me put my stuff down—what is this, secret police? Should I surrender?
“Why come to school if you’re going to run away? If you wanted to skip, you wouldn’t come at all.”
“You’re so sly! You actually ran away last time. I won’t listen to a scumbag like you anymore!”
“Eh… really?”
That’s quite a judgment. Apparently, Ijuuin trusts me very little. She used to call me with honorifics, but now she drops them. How did it come to this?
“Listen, Kuzuhara! Obey Ijuuin-san!”
“We won’t forgive Kuzuhara, who’s trying to ruin ‘Damenzu’!”
While I was getting fed up with this distrustful princess, a few boys including Sayama and Gotou voiced their support.
They had become Ijuuin’s followers and formed an unofficial ‘Damenzu’ fan club at school, openly opposing me.
“Guys…”
I couldn’t help but press my temples. Dealing with Ijuuin alone was tough, and now the boys had turned completely against me. It was sad in many ways.
Did Ijuuin have that much charisma, or were Sayama and the others just gullible? Maybe both.
Seeing my former friends’ downfall made me look at them coldly, which was understandable.
“Do you have no pride? Relying on newly transferred Ijuuin, you all look like foxes borrowing the tiger’s might.”
“Shut up! Do you understand our feelings? You touched my Setsuna! I worked so hard to get arena seats at the last concert! Do you know how much I worked part-time!?”

“Yeah! We supported Arisa and bought tons of goods for them! I thought I was contributing to ‘Damenzu,’ but when I found out the money went to a scumbag like you, Kuzuhara, I almost lost my mind! My brain almost exploded! Total brain destruction!!!”
Well, even if they’re angry, that’s just how society is…
Buying goods is a personal choice and ultimately one’s own responsibility.
It’s good for me since I get pocket money from Setsuna and the others, but it’s not like I’m pocketing all the money fans spend on ‘Damenzu.’
There are various rights and fees involved with goods and concert tickets, most of which go to the venue.
The money fans give to ‘Dimension Stars!’ is distributed among various companies, including the agency Setsuna and others belong to, and the idols’ salaries are only a small fraction.
Many fans dislike the idea of idols being called products, but if you remove that psychological filter, it’s a very accurate way to look at it.

Customers find value in the product called ‘Dimension Stars!’ and buy it, increasing demand and spawning more derivative goods, which customers buy again. This cycle circulates funds, boosting the economy and popularity.
What I’m saying is, many people besides me profit from ‘Damenzu.’
They don’t stand out but probably do countless shady things behind the scenes.
What I do is just receiving money from Setsuna and the others, and I have no plans to commit crimes since I won’t work.
Wait? Doesn’t that make me the cleanest person ever?
I think I’m handling money more properly than anyone else.
I’m not bad at all, right???
“That’s not true! Don’t change the subject! What you’re doing is basically being a kept man, and you’re nothing but scum!”
“Hey, don’t respond to my inner voice.”
Even if I’m a manga-like character, adding psychic powers to a blonde stalker princess is too much. I can’t keep up.
(Still no good… I thought I could pull it off.)
Convincing a wealthy heiress is hard.
What to do now? But help came from the other side.
“Kazu-kun! Is it okay now? Come over here and talk! Arisa-chan’s here too!”
The one smiling and waving was my childhood friend and savior, Setsuna.
Arisa was also watching me from her desk, resting her cheek on her hand. It seemed the two childhood friends were finally together in the classroom.
“Oh, Setsuna and Arisa! You’re here! Wait for me, I’m coming!”
I couldn’t miss this chance. I gratefully accepted their rescue.
Even Ijuuin and the fan club guys didn’t say anything to Setsuna and Arisa. They just glared at me with frustration but didn’t try to stop me.
Walking boldly between them, I snorted softly.
“Hmph… Sorry, Ijuuin. Setsuna’s calling me. See ya. Being needed by the idols themselves is tough.”
“You guys call me scum, but Setsuna and the others want to talk to me! Being needed and called with a smile even though I’m scum is tough! Ahahaha!”
““You scumbag…!””
“Kuzuhara Kazuma!”
Hmph, I’m not scared of those bloodshot eyes, Ijuuin and her followers.
After all, I have the idols on my side. The murderous aura from a wealthy heiress feels almost pleasant.
I feel like I’ve risen to the upper class. I’m a bit of a social climber.
“Fuhahaha! Goodbye, commoners! I’m different from you!”
Walking under the jealous gazes of classmates who are just fans, unlike me who’s sought after by childhood friend idols, felt great.
